column2: I have decided to hold great wargames. Riders will race across the plain, archers will loose at full gallop, and blades will ring in the ring of shields. Every warrior of my realm who thinks themselves the best will have the chance to prove it before the whole horde.
It will be a great contest.

To my faithful warrior [Root.GetDynName],

I shall expect you at the wargames to be held at [From.Capital.GetName]. Bring your best horse and your best bow, and leave your excuses at home.

[From.GetFullName]
I will saddle my horse at once!
I do not have the time.

[Root.GetTitledFirstName],

I regret that I cannot come to the wargames.

[From.GetTitledName]
More glory for the rest of us, then!

Warriors have ridden to my camp from every corner of the realm. Horses stamp and toss their heads, the crowd roars on the slopes around the field, and the champions raise their weapons to me in salute. I lift my hand, and let it fall: the games begin.
May the best warrior win!

I have come to the camp of the [From.PrimaryTitle.GetRulerTitle] for the wargames. Horses stamp and toss their heads, the crowd roars on the slopes around the field, and I raise my weapon in salute to [From.GetTitledFirstName]. [From.GetSheHeCap] lifts a hand, and lets it fall: the games begin.
I shall give it my all!
No rider was faster, no arrow truer and no blade quicker than mine today: I have won the wargames! [From.GetTitledFirstName] hands me the prize before the cheering horde.
I knew I would win!
[From.GetFullName] has won the wargames. No rider, archer or swordsman could match [From.GetHerHim] today.
A worthy winner.
Sky Burial

As my father's heir, it falls to me to carry him to the mountains. He will be laid out for the birds of prey, and in death he will give his flesh to every living thing that hungers. May his spirit soar to the heavens.

As my mother's heir, it falls to me to carry her to the mountains. She will be laid out for the birds of prey, and in death she will give her flesh to every living thing that hungers. May her spirit soar to the heavens.

My brother left no heirs of his own, so it falls to me to carry him to the mountains. He will be laid out for the birds of prey, and in death he will give his flesh to every living thing that hungers. May his spirit soar to the heavens.

My sister left no heirs of her own, so it falls to me to carry her to the mountains. She will be laid out for the birds of prey, and in death she will give her flesh to every living thing that hungers. May her spirit soar to the heavens.

As the custom is, I must carry my predecessor to the mountains, to be laid out for the birds of prey. In death they will give their flesh to every living thing that hungers. May their spirit soar to the heavens.
I shall carry the body to the mountains myself.
A sky burial is prepared.
No. A lord so great deserves a golden tomb.
Work begins on a great hidden tomb.
Not the birds. The Great Maw shall have this one!
A long and dangerous journey over the mountains to the land of the Ogres. Those in poor health would likely die on the way...
Storm in the Foothills
On the road to the mountains a storm sweeps down on us out of a black sky. Cold rain lashes the column, the ground turns to mud under the hooves, and the wind tugs at the shroud of the dead.
We find shelter and wait for it to pass.
A little rain never killed anyone. Ride on!
A Lone Hermit

On the road to the mountains we come upon a hermit. He owns little but a patched tent, an old and sickly horse and a handful of sheep, yet the scarred old man still invites me to share salted tea with him. As we talk I find, to my surprise, that I am enjoying his company. He has seen more battles than most of my warriors.
Here. Take this.
Why not ride with us, old warrior?
My thanks, but I must be going.
Sky Burial

High among the bare peaks I lay the body on a flat stone open to the sky, and speak the old words over it. The vultures are already circling as I chant. By the time we have started back down the slope, they are tearing at the flesh with beak and claw, carrying the dead into the heavens a mouthful at a time.
Go to [Root.Religion.GetRandomGodName] now.
Being Followed

Ever since we left the mountains I have had the feeling that something is following me, but whenever I turn there is nothing there. Then, at the top of a rise, I spin round in the saddle and catch it: one of the vultures from the burial, gliding low behind me. And not just any vulture, but a great bearded vulture, the bone-breaker of the high peaks!
Can I keep it?!
Scare it away.
Digging the Tomb
I have chosen a remote and secret valley for the tomb. The diggers stand ready with their picks and baskets, waiting for my word.
Well then. Put your backs into it!
The Golden Tomb

The tomb is finished, glittering with the gold and steel of a lifetime's plunder. We seal it and cover it, and take care that no marker betrays where it lies. Then the diggers are put to the sword, every one, so that no one but I and my guard will ever know where to find it.
Magnificent. No one shall ever disturb it.
Now kill the guards as well.
The Road to the Great Maw

For weeks we have climbed through the passes towards the land of the Ogres. Our water is low, our food lower, and the body has begun to rot: we can smell it from the far end of the column. The Great Maw that the Ogres worship is still days away, and my riders beg me to turn back before the mountains swallow us all.
Nonsense! We go on!
This was a bad idea... Let us turn back.

At last we stand at the edge of the Great Maw: a pit so vast the far side is lost in haze, ringed with the gnawed bones of a thousand offerings. The ground trembles as if something below is chewing. I tip what is left of the body over the edge, and the rumbling deepens, and I swear I hear it swallow.
A worthy burial! Now for home...
Reach home safely.
That was something! But now I must rest... right here...
Home at Last

It was a terrible journey, but I made it home. Most of my riders lie dead in the passes, and of those who came back few will ever be the same. I alone seem to have come through it no worse, and perhaps somewhat harder.
What does not kill me makes me stronger!

My warriors and I are wrestling to keep fit for war when a crowd begins to gather. Wrestling is an old and honoured custom among the riders, and every so often a training bout turns into a show. My warriors are already strutting for the crowd, and now they beckon to me to join them.
I can't disappoint them, can I?
You step into the ring.
No time for games. Back to drill, the lot of you!
Have your fun. I will sit this one out...

A proper bout can last hours: it tests endurance more than strength. The wrestlers dance into the ring and dance out again, and the winner must help the loser up from the dirt when it is over. Whoever I face, I know I will have to give everything I have.
I challenge the best of my warriors!
Is challenged to a wrestling bout!
I challenge my trusty steed, Glitterhoof!
Whoever I challenge will yield, naturally.
On second thought, this looks dangerous...

The crowd roars as my opponent and I dance into the ring. We circle, then lock together, straining chest to chest. Minutes pass in furious grappling until I feel [From.GetHerHim] tire. I let go of the shoulders, seize the legs and tip [From.GetHerHim] over. [From.GetSheHeCap] hits the dirt: I have won!
Pathetic. I won't help [From.GetHerHim] up!
Victory! Now take my hand, I'll help you up.
I may have won, but we'll share the glory!
That was thrilling. Come to my tent later?

The crowd roars as my opponent and I dance into the ring. We circle, then lock together, straining chest to chest. Minutes pass in furious grappling, and slowly I feel my strength drain away. Then [From.GetSheHe] catches me off balance, seizes my legs, lifts me clean off the ground and drops me in the dirt. I am beaten!
I lost, but what a bout!
Beaten fair and square. A worthy opponent.
You dare defeat your lord? Now feel my wrath!
I lost, but... come to my tent later?
